summary:
Banten stands under Indonesia's national framework on gender identity and documentation. Since June 2021 the Indonesian Ministry of Home Affairs has conducted outreach to issue identity papers, including the electronic identity card (e-KTP), to transgender Indonesians, and Banten is named among the nine provinces where this has operated, alongside West Java, Central Java, East Java, North Sumatra, South Sumatra, South Sulawesi, Lampung and Papua.

The stated reasoning for the outreach was that many transgender people in these provinces were undocumented, particularly where families did not approve of their transition. For a trans visitor in Banten this bears on document status and enrolment: the province is one where identity-document issuance for transgender residents has been carried out since mid-2021.
tangentialFactors: An August 2026 feature reports growing repression against Indonesia's transgender community nationally, which sets the wider climate in which Banten's document-outreach programme operates.
localsOnly: Transgender residents of Banten have been within the scope of the Ministry of Home Affairs' identity-document outreach since June 2021, one of nine provinces covered. The programme was directed at transgender people who lacked documentation, including those whose families did not approve of their transition.
outOfScopeNotes: The source inventory does not document how many transgender residents of Banten have actually received identity papers under the outreach, nor whether the programme is ongoing or concluded. No Banten-specific enforcement incidents, provincial regulations, or facility-access rules for trans visitors were identified in the inventory.
